newsitem.title: FRANCE: French parliamentary panel to study auto industry.
newsitem.headline: French parliamentary panel to study auto industry.

text.p: The National Assembly named a special commission on Wednesday to study the automobile industry's future in France and in Europe.
Communist deputy Daniel Paul will head the 45-member commission, which will hold its first meeting on August 27, parliamentary aides said.
Twenty-five of the panel's members are from the assembly's leftist majority, a coalition of Socialists, Communists and Greens.

The commission was created at the request of the Socialist bloc of deputies after loss-making French carmaker Renault abruptly announced plans earlier this year to close an assembly plant in Vilvoorde, Belgium, employing 3,100 people.

Renault, which is 46-percent owned by the French state, argued that closing the plant was a competitive necessity but politicians in both France and Belgium attacked the move as inappropriate during a time of high unemployment.
Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin pledged during this year's parliamentary election campaign to review the case.
But following his review he allowed the plant closing to go forward after winning assurances there would be no layoffs.
